title: Office Relocation Checklist Newcastle: From Lease Decision to First Working Day
excerpt: Connect the lease decision, FitOut, furniture, technology and move with clear owners. Use this stage-based checklist around your actual documents, premises and supplier dates.
author: Joe Kelley
metaTitle: Office Relocation Checklist Newcastle | Your Office Space
metaDescription: Plan a Newcastle office relocation with confirmed lease dates, a clear budget, supplier responsibilities, site access and first-day readiness checks.
body:
## How do you plan an office relocation?

Start with the business requirements and confirmed lease dates, then connect the premises decision with the work needed to operate at the next site. Assign owners for the budget, appointments, delivery decisions, technology, furniture and move.

This Newcastle and Hunter checklist follows project stages rather than universal month-by-month deadlines. Your actual lease provisions, premises, supplier availability and operating requirements determine the programme. Ask your solicitor to confirm legal dates and obligations against the documents.

## 1. Confirm the lease position and the decision

- Gather the signed lease, amendments and relevant landlord correspondence.
- Ask your solicitor to confirm expiry, any applicable notice requirements and questions about leaving or renewing.
- Identify the people who can approve premises, expenditure and appointments.
- Test renewal, relocation or purchase against the business brief rather than assuming a move is the only answer.

**Helpful tip:** record the source and owner of each date. Keep an uncertain date visibly unconfirmed until checked.

[Organise your lease critical dates](/tools/critical-dates)

[Compare renewal with relocation](/blog/renew-or-relocate-commercial-lease)

## 2. Define the workplace brief and whole-project budget

Record peak attendance, activities, meeting needs, storage, visitor access, preferred locations and essential operating requirements. List existing furniture and equipment you hope to retain, with suitability still to be assessed.

Separate ongoing occupancy costs from initial works, consultants, furniture, technology, moving, possible overlap between sites and existing lease exit work. Record the assumptions, exclusions, GST basis and approvals needed for each allowance.

**Helpful tip:** separate essentials from preferences and nominate an internal decision owner. That helps resolve trade-offs when layouts, costs or timing change.

[Prepare a Newcastle tenant representation brief](/blog/tenant-representation-brief-newcastle)

[Compare commercial lease assumptions](/resources/lease-comparison)

## 3. Assess the actual premises and building access

For every shortlisted Newcastle, Lake Macquarie or Hunter property, check the actual building arrangements. A suburb name or building style does not establish the loading, lift, access or services available.

- Ask about delivery routes, dimensions, loading and lift bookings.
- Identify occupied areas, operating-hour limits and any staging requirements.
- Gather available plans and building information for the appointed advisers.
- Clarify landlord requirements and who will assess the proposed use and relevant approval pathway.
- Check the work needed before furniture, IT and staff can arrive.

**Helpful tip:** give the removalist and installation team the site-specific access information before confirming their scopes. Record unresolved access questions alongside the programme.

[Explore client-side office FitOut project management](/office-fitout)

## 4. Agree the workstreams and supplier dates

Appoint the appropriate consultants, contractors and suppliers for the actual scope. Confirm which work sits with the client, landlord, appointed contractor, IT provider, furniture supplier and removalist.

Obtain supplier-specific availability and delivery information rather than using a generic furniture or fibre lead time. Connect installation dates with the readiness of the site, power, data and access arrangements.

| Workstream | Useful confirmation | Owner to identify |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Building work | Scope, appointments, dependencies and access | Appointed contractors and client decision maker |
| Furniture | Specifications, quantities, retained items and installation scope | Furniture supplier and client approver |
| Technology | Services, equipment, cutover and testing plan | Client IT team and appointed providers |
| Moving | Inventory, labels, access, staging and operating limits | Removalist and move coordinator |
| Site readiness | Handover actions, documents and outstanding work | Relevant project team members and client owner |

**Helpful tip:** maintain a single decision register with the person responsible and the date each answer is needed. A supplier's proposed date should not silently become an approved move date.

[Plan commercial furniture supply and installation](/furniture)

[Prepare the furniture installation scope](/blog/office-furniture-installation-checklist-newcastle)

## 5. Plan continuity and communications

Agree where staff will work during changeovers, who can resolve issues and how the business will communicate changes. Have the appropriate internal owners identify address, registration, insurance, account and directory updates relevant to the business.

Confirm access arrangements at both premises, test the proposed IT cutover sequence and establish what happens if an essential service is not ready. Keep responsibilities for keys, cards, equipment and confidential material clear.

**Helpful tip:** label items by destination room or zone and use the same names on the layout and move plan. Give staff a clear contact for questions before the move.

## 6. Test the first working day before relying on it

Check what staff need to operate: access, connectivity, phones, meeting systems, equipment, furniture and storage. Record outstanding defects, documents and actions, with an owner for each.

A finished-looking office does not establish that all project requirements or business systems are ready. The appointed contractors and advisers confirm requirements within their scopes; the client also needs to test the operational tasks its team relies on.

**Helpful tip:** walk through a normal staff and visitor journey, from entering the building to joining a call or using a meeting room. Log what prevents the task from working.

[Use the office FitOut handover checklist](/blog/office-fitout-handover-checklist)

For eligible Newcastle CBD and Lake Macquarie premises, [plan commercial cleaning](/cleaning) as a separately agreed scope, including the site, timing and access requirements.

## 7. Close the outgoing site and review the new workplace

Work with your solicitor and appointed providers to clarify the outgoing lease responsibilities, agreed work and documents required. Track outstanding commercial and project actions rather than assuming they finish automatically on move day.

At the new site, ask staff what is working and what needs attention. Assign owners for adjustments, supplier issues and ongoing workplace care. Record the next confirmed lease dates so the information remains available after the project ends.

**Helpful tip:** retain the approved layouts, supplier contacts, handover documents and open-action register in a shared location with a clear owner.

## Where YOS can help

YOS supports tenant-side commercial leasing in NSW and provides client-side FitOut project management within the agreed appointment. YOS is not the builder or head contractor; appointed contractors perform construction and trade work. Furniture and eligible local cleaning are separately defined workstreams, with scope and responsibilities confirmed before work begins.

[Discuss your Newcastle lease decision](/tenant-rep/newcastle#newcastle-enquiry), or [send a FitOut project brief](/office-fitout#fitout-enquiry) if the premises and delivery work are your next priority.

For an existing lease, [start a free Lease Health Check](/lease-health-check). Uploading your current lease is optional and further advisory work is scoped separately.

You can also [send your relocation enquiry](#blog-contact-form) with the location, lease dates and project stage you know. We can confirm the information needed for the next step.
